end.summary:
Aarav ordered BCE and CE dates on a timeline in several examples.
They practised that BCE years count down toward 1 BCE; the earlier mix-up was corrected later.
They discussed archaeological remains, inscriptions, texts, and oral traditions as historical sources.
They continued to treat inscriptions as more complete or reliable than other sources; this was not corrected by the end.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised timeline ordering with BCE and CE dates, using examples and correction of the BCE counting direction. Aarav gave several correct date sequences and connected burnt rice remains with what people ate. They mixed up the idea that one inscription can tell the whole story; this was still present at the end. At home, ask them to match each source—pottery, inscription, text, and oral tradition—with one question it can answer, then explain why sources are compared.
